mechanism_narrative: The observed upward trend in RETAIL_REC mobility over the last three weeks, despite remaining negative, indicates a gradual return of consumer activity that will continue to improve RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days, indicating a reversal of the observed recovery trend.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained high level of GROCERY_PHARM mobility, consistently above 5% baseline, suggests increased essential outings and a general comfort with public spaces, which will spill over into non-essential retail activity over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above 5% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining above 5% for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility, coupled with a decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility, signifies a shift from home-based activities to out-of-home work and commuting, which will drive higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise while RESIDENTIAL falls week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the last 28 days, even if WORKPLACES and TRANSIT increase and RESIDENTIAL decreases.

mechanism_narrative: Under a regime of easing restrictions, the continued recovery of PARKS mobility indicates increasing public confidence and willingness to leave home for leisure, which will translate into higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as more non-essential venues open.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not show an upward trend over the next 28 days, despite PARKS mobility continuing its recovery under easing restrictions.

mechanism_narrative: The persistently high RESIDENTIAL mobility, despite a slight recent dip, suggests a continued preference for staying home, which will suppress out-of-home activities and lead to lower RETAIL_REC over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is higher than the average of the last 7 days, despite RESIDENTIAL mobility remaining above 8%.

mechanism_narrative: The recent week-on-week drop in WORKPLACES mobility, if it falls below -30% from baseline, signals a reversal in the return-to-office trend, leading to reduced weekday foot traffic and consequently lower RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -30% from baseline week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days, even if WORKPLACES mobility drops below -30% from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous and sustained recovery in both GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS mobility indicates a broad increase in public comfort with out-of-home activities, suggesting a positive spillover effect on RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS both show week-on-week increases for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the last 28 days, despite both GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS showing sustained increases.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of tightening restrictions, any further week-on-week decline in TRANSIT mobility indicates reduced essential and non-essential travel, directly leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next week due to decreased accessibility.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls by more than 2 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 7 days, despite TRANSIT mobility declining by more than 2 points week-on-week under tightening restrictions.
